messages:
Olivia: Quick design question — small change to the rollback flow. Thinking about a "revert guard" toast pattern + focused SR announce instead of keeping the destructive Rollback button inline. Want feedback on copy, a11y, and edge cases. Figma mock: https://figma.com/file/abcd1234

Dario: Love the idea. How would this play with canary pause? If we show a toast and user navigates to another panel they might miss the undo window :thinking_face:

Jamal: Toast can be persistent until dismissed or until the user navigates away. For SR announce my gut is `aria-live="assertive"` for immediate feedback — but we can test. Also ensure the toast has a visible focusable button for keyboard users.

Sara: Copy options: "Reverted to v3.2.1 — traffic restored. Undo" vs "Rollback complete — view changes". Which communicates action better to PMs/support?

Kevin: @Sara I prefer: "Reverted to v3.2.1. View changes · Undo" — put emphasis on viewing what changed, keep Undo as a secondary action.

Olivia: Accessibility notes: when toast appears we should either move focus into it (so screen reader users get it immediately) OR provide an SR-only helper that tells users "Rollback complete — press Tab to access Undo." We need to decide. Also `Esc` should dismiss.

design-bot: Accessibility checklist updated for this thread: focus management, aria-live region, contrast of CTA buttons.

Dario: Concern re accidental trigger — propose a threshold: if the rollback target currently has >50% traffic, open a small confirm modal; otherwise quick rollback via menu -> toast with 10s Undo snackbar.

Sara: Modal for big rollbacks seems reasonable. Modal copy should be explicit: "Confirm rollback — this will restore traffic to version 3.2.1 and cannot be undone from this dialog." Add a secondary undo in the toast if we keep both flows.

Kevin: Microcopy nit: should we call it "Undo" or "Restore traffic"? "Undo" is concise but might be ambiguous for non-technical users.

Olivia: I'm leaning to keep short verb "Undo" in the toast and surface a fuller label in the modal (e.g., "Confirm: Revert traffic to v3.2.1"). Also add an icon (undo/shield) to help quick scan.

Jamal: For SR announce example, we can use: `aria-live="assertive"` text: "Deployment reverted to version 3.2.1. 100% traffic restored. Undo available." That covers state + action.

Sara: Edge case: if user is typing in a form inside console, moving focus to toast can be disruptive. Alternate approach: do not forcibly move focus, but ensure toast is reachable and SR-announced. Provide an SR-only note: "Action available — press Tab to focus notification."

Kevin: Visual treatment: soft red/orange left accent, neutral background, confirm button with strong color. Check contrast of text + button per WCAG.

Olivia: Implementation variants I'm going to mock: 1) toast + focus move (assertive), 2) toast + SR hint (no focus move), 3) modal for >50% traffic. Will post Figma variants and recommended keyboard flows.

Dario: :thumbsup: I'll run an accessibility pass on the variants once posted.

Sara: Also add a unit/integration test for the console that asserts the announcement string and presence of Undo button in DOM.

Kevin: One more infra note — add analytics: `rollback.initiated`, `rollback.completed`, `rollback.undone` with payload including priorVersion, targetVersion, trafficPercent.

Olivia: Great — I'll file a design ticket (D-2207) with the mock, copy options, and the a11y checklist. Will link the ticket + Figma here when ready.

Sara: Thanks — really like this direction.

Kevin: Thanks all, convenient UX and safer surface for rollbacks :+1:

Olivia: Posting Figma & ticket in #design-updates after lunch.
